title: Experimental and numerical simulation study of tensile mechanical properties of corroded carbon steel utilizing galvanostatic corrosion and 3D scanning
abstract: Non-uniform corrosion poses a significant threat to structural safety. This paper proposes a method to consider the effect of non-uniform corrosion on corroded steel members, utilizing 3D scanning and reverse modeling techniques. The degradation of the tensile mechanical properties of corroded carbon steel is studied using both numerical and experimental methods. Galvanostatic corrosion method was adopted to efficiently obtain corroded specimens with varying weight loss ratio. By utilizing 3D scanning, the geometry of corrosion topography is reverse modeled, and corrosion depth is statistically analyzed through fine meshing. Standard tensile tests reveal that non-uniform corrosion significantly impacts the mechanical properties of the specimens. The reduction in ultimate bearing capacity of corroded specimens exceeded the change in weight loss ratio. As the weight loss ratio increases, the failure modes of specimens primarily shift to brittle failure, indicating a significant decrease in ductility performance. An improved bearing capacity prediction formula based on traditional weight loss ratio method is proposed. Refined finite element simulation of the experiments verified that corrosion does not affect the material constitutive behavior.
